title: Capacity-Adjusted Resilience Prioritization (CARP): RICE + Cost/Latency Resilience Multiplier
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce CARP (Capacity-Adjusted Resilience Prioritization), a pragmatic extension of RICE designed for inference-first platforms. CARP adds two operational modifiers to standard RICE: a resilience multiplier (captures SLO/availability risk and fallback complexity) and a capacity-adjustment factor (captures Dedicated/Private capacity constraints and cost elasticity). The goal is to provide a single score product + infra teams can use to prioritize features that trade off latency, cost, reliability, and capacity commitments.
acceptance_criteria: A decision-ready CARP scoring spreadsheet with worked examples for 8 representative initiatives (hosted feature, dedicated-only optimization, private deployment compliance, runtime kernel change, console UX, autoscaler flow, caching product, evals infra)
A Confluence spec describing CARP math, when to use it vs vanilla RICE, and guidance for setting resilience multiplier and capacity-adjustment factors
Reusable script (single-table CSV -> CARP score) and a short how-to in the Console docs team repo
Stakeholder buy-in: Product, Runtime Eng, Infra (Dedicated), and Sales/Customer Success signoff recorded in comments
One pilot prioritization run applied to Q2 roadmap producing a ranked list and 2 sensitivity scenarios (high-cost pressure, high-latency-risk)
updates: 2026-02-26: Draft formula proposed in kickoff: CARP = ((Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort) * ResilienceMultiplier * CapacityAdjustment / CostPenalty. Shared with runtime and infra for feedback.

2026-03-01: Infra feedback (A. Gupta): requested clearer guidance for CapacityAdjustment values for Dedicated capacity (reserved vs burst). Action: add lookup table and example for 1 GPU pool and 4 GPU pool customers.

2026-03-04: Product review (S. Ramirez): suggested merge of CostPenalty into CapacityAdjustment as a single economic friction term; retained separate CostPenalty to preserve interpretability for PMs. Agreed to keep both but document rationale.

2026-03-06: Engineering review (L. O'Neill): asked for an observability signal mapping (SLO breach probability -> ResilienceMultiplier). Added a recommended mapping: low risk=1.0, medium=0.8, high=0.5 for features with fallback complexity.

2026-03-09: Created CARP worked examples spreadsheet (Drive link). Pilot set includes: streaming batching optimization, KV-prefix cache, quantization profiling, autoscaler policy, rollout UX for canaries, embedding batching, private VPC onboarding, enhanced audit logs.

2026-03-11: Ran pilot prioritization workshop with 10 stakeholders (Product, Runtime, Dedicated Eng, Solutions). Outcome: CARP ordering differed from RICE on two items where capacity friction changed ranking — noted in meeting notes and captured action items.
2026-03-12: PRD and Confluence draft uploaded for cross-team review. Requested signoff by 2026-03-16 to meet roadmap planning deadline.

2026-03-14: Received legal feedback noting audit-logs rollout may require privacy review for EU customers. Marked that sub-issue needs security_review_required flag. Awaiting Security team's estimate.
2026-03-14: Updated formula to include floor for CapacityAdjustment (min 0.4) to prevent edge-case inflation of low-effort, extremely constrained items. Documented trade-offs.
